title: Luxor to Aswan: the classic 4-night route
standfirst: The most popular Nile cruise: four nights upstream from Luxor to Aswan, past Esna, Edfu and Kom Ombo. Here is how the days usually run. For other routes, see [[up]].

sections.heading: Why it takes four nights
paragraphs: The ship sails against the current and must pass the lock at Esna, where ships often queue. The extra night gives time for both banks at Luxor before setting off.

sections.heading: What you see
paragraphs: At Luxor, the temples of Karnak and Luxor on the East Bank and the Valley of the Kings and Hatshepsut’s temple on the West Bank. Upstream, the Temple of Horus at Edfu and the double temple at Kom Ombo. At Aswan, the High Dam, the Unfinished Obelisk and Philae.

sections.heading: Good to know
paragraphs: Embarkation is usually around midday on the first day in Luxor, and check-out is after breakfast on the last day in Aswan. The order of visits can change with the lock queue and opening hours, but every site is still covered.

faqs.q: Is four nights enough for Luxor and Aswan?
faqs.a: For the main sites, yes. Many travellers add a night in Aswan or Luxor before or after.
Yes, as an optional excursion from Aswan, usually early in the morning of the last full day.
